video_title: Pablo Torre says Clippers' punishment from NBA could have been more | Dan Patrick Show | NBA on NBC

quotes.speaker: Pablo Torre
quotes.summary_phrase: Internal politics of the Clippers' league governance and salary cap circumvention
quotes.excerpt: What does the internal politics of league governance look like when you have a scope that leads to a rabbit hole?
quotes.quote: The thing that was interesting yesterday was just what the NBA would do about it. And that is what we found out. What does the internal politics of league governance look like when you have a scope that leads to a rabbit hole that has four separate companies in it, manufactured paper trails, fake jobs, not just for Kawhi Leonard, but for the companies, like fake consulting jobs for the companies that funneled money to Kawhi Leonard through the Clippers as well as those companies?

quotes.speaker: Pablo Torre
quotes.summary_phrase: Steve Ballmer's punishment for salary cap circumvention was unprecedented
quotes.excerpt: The biggest punishment for an owner that we've ever seen in American sports, I think.
quotes.quote: I thought that it could have been more. The biggest punishment for an owner that we've ever seen in American sports, I think, when you account for the fact that it is Steve Ballmer banned from the building for a year, his head of business banned from the building for a year, his head of basketball banned from the building for six months because Lawrence Frank, that basketball ops president, participated and provided contemporaneous notes to the NBA, by the way, a whole other rabbit hole of why was Lawrence Frank taking notes during the cap circumvention meetings in which he is quoting Steve Ballmer talking about how he's going to service Dennis Robertson and Kawhi Leonard to circumvent the cap.

quotes.speaker: Pablo Torre
quotes.summary_phrase: Steve Ballmer's letter to Adam Silver blaming the podcast for the investigation
quotes.excerpt: He has written a letter via his very expensive attorneys to Adam Silver blaming this podcaster.
quotes.quote: Steve Ballmer has written a letter via his very expensive attorneys to Adam Silver blaming this podcaster for getting the NBA to do a prejudiced investigation. And at first, after the ruling came out, he threatened arbitration. But this is something that is very interesting that I don't know if people appreciate about what the NBA did. When the NBA tried to settle with Steve Ballmer and they said, hey, we have a narrow scope, we have undeniable evidence, we want to just make sure that you have the opportunity to take your punishment, admit wrongdoing, and let us all move on, Steve Ballmer decided to fight.

quotes.speaker: Pablo Torre
quotes.summary_phrase: Kawhi Leonard's fine and the impact on the Clippers' salary cap
quotes.excerpt: When Kawhi gets a slap on the wrist, that's where the slap on the wrist was, Dan.
quotes.quote: When Kawhi gets a slap on the wrist, that's where the slap on the wrist was, Dan. $700,000 for Kawhi Leonard. Historically, that's quite a bit, but in terms of the role he had in the whole story, that's a slap on the wrist. He can now go on to Toronto and the betting lines can adjust based on that, if Toronto wants to go through with this, not knowing what else is in the box.

quotes.speaker: Pablo Torre
quotes.summary_phrase: Arbitration is off the table, but Steve Ballmer can sue the NBA
quotes.excerpt: Arbitration, because of that settlement, is off the table. Can't go to arbitration.
quotes.quote: In the NBA, what Adam Silver knows better than Steve Ballmer and his lawyers know apparently is that arbitration can only be activated by the union. And so arbitration, because of that settlement, is off the table. Can't go to arbitration. What can Steve Ballmer do? He can literally sue the NBA. He can sue Adam Silver, he can sue me, he can sue Wachtell Lipton, he can sue you, he can sue everybody. And that opens the door to, spoiler alert, more discovery of documents.

quotes.speaker: Pablo Torre
quotes.summary_phrase: Steve Ballmer's public lies about the investigation and the NBA's fact-checking
quotes.excerpt: Take time out of your day to rewatch what Steve Ballmer did after knowing what he actually did.
quotes.quote: Take time out of your day to rewatch what Steve Ballmer did after knowing what he actually did. And you will see that he is lying repeatedly. And once he does that, and he's on the record lying in public about what happened here, the NBA now has the ability to fact-check, as I did, as I have been doing this whole time.

quotes.speaker: Pablo Torre
quotes.summary_phrase: Pablo Torre is not currently targeting Jalen Brunson and the Knicks
quotes.excerpt: I am not currently targeting, I am not currently looking into, I am not currently circling Jalen Brunson.
quotes.quote: I am not currently targeting, I am not currently looking into, I am not currently circling Jalen Brunson and the Knicks. I have had all sorts of calls about so many teams. I have talked to people on the Knicks about all of this, and they are just not the focus because we have other things that are, by the way, coming very soon that are in the vein of what are billionaires who run sports trying to get away with using your money.

quotes.speaker: Pablo Torre
quotes.summary_phrase: Steve Ballmer's ambitious salary cap circumvention scheme
quotes.excerpt: He had the ambition of creating a scheme that is beyond what other owners have attempted.
quotes.quote: He had the ambition of creating a scheme that is beyond what other owners have attempted. That much I am very comfortable saying. This is the furthest point in the spectrum of attempted salary cap circumvention. People do it by degree, no one did it by this order of magnitude, and that's why the NBA, which wanted to make everybody stop talking about this, that's why they had to do the thing we saw yesterday.

quotes.speaker: Pablo Torre
quotes.summary_phrase: The Clippers fed ESPN a story that may not have been true
quotes.excerpt: ESPN had done, according to my reporting, is they were fed a story by the Clippers.
quotes.quote: What ESPN had done, according to my reporting, is they were fed a story by the Clippers that the Clippers may have known was not true. And why do you do that? Well, perhaps it's because that's the available territory that you have, having been beaten on the other part of this landscape. Perhaps you really believed it because the Clippers look you in the eye and for months, for a year, said to you, we're telling the truth, that annoying clout-chasing podcaster is lying to you.

quotes.speaker: Pablo Torre
quotes.summary_phrase: Breakdown of the total value of the Clippers' salary cap circumvention
quotes.excerpt: Aspiration had a total value of $48 million.
quotes.quote: Aspiration had a total value of $48 million. Now let's bring in the other companies, right? Boingo Wireless, of course, which is just funny because, of course, the wireless provider of the Intuit Dome is giving Kawhi Leonard payments off the books. Of course, Dactronics, the scoreboard operator is, of course, Locked In Insurance, the insurance company on the construction of the dome is doing the same thing, Dan. Those three companies, according to the NBA's investigation through 2021, guaranteed $18 million to Kawhi Leonard. So doing the math, that's $66 million only through, let's call it 2022.

quotes.speaker: Pablo Torre
quotes.summary_phrase: Kawhi Leonard's contract extension with the Clippers
quotes.excerpt: He resigns with the Clippers, as I've said before on my show, in January of '24 for a discount.
quotes.quote: He resigns with the Clippers, as I've said before on my show, in January of '24 for a discount. A discount, less than the max. Why and what happened there? And so you're at 66 million plus. I've told the story, the beginning of it, around the Rhode Island Football Club, starting in LLC, in which he got secret undisclosed equity the week before he signed the extension. And I ask, as always, what else was there? And I have a feeling, as always, that there is more.
